step.text:
Looking at Electron 33's notification implementation, the `Show()` method closes any existing notification before creating a new one through the presenter, generating a unique ID for it. The `Notification` class itself is wrapped with cleanup-at-exit semantics, which handles garbage collection when the process terminates.

There's a known issue where notification click events don't fire if the JS wrapper gets garbage collected — the native observer gets destroyed along with it. On macOS specifically, when the JS object is GC'd, the destructor calls `set_delegate(nullptr)` and destroys the notification, which on older macOS versions would remove it from the notification center entirely. But since Jamel can still click the notification, it's likely either not being GC'd or the banner persists on screen even after removal from the delivered list. With newer UNUserNotificationCenter (macOS 11+, used in Electron v25+), the behavior around notification removal might differ.

The symptom — "clicking just hides the notification" — is exactly what happens when the app receives no click callback: macOS dismisses the banner on click by default without the delegate firing. If the `click` event were actually firing, `openWindow()` would focus the window, which Jamel would definitely notice. Since he reports nothing happens, the click event isn't being triggered at all.

Two main possibilities: either the Notification object is being garbage collected because no reference is held, or macOS isn't routing the default action to an unsigned dev-run app — though if that were the case, Jamel wouldn't be seeing the notification appear in the first place.

I'm leaning toward the GC issue. The fix would be to hold a reference to each notification until it's closed or clicked, then release it. I should also check how the app handles the window creation timing and whether the renderer is ready when the notification fires. Let me look at the test coverage for alerts and see if there's a main-process test harness, and also verify how Electron 33 handles notification garbage collection.

+ export type Box = { left: number; width: number }
+ 
+ const end = (box: Box) => box.left + box.width
+ const middle = (box: Box) => box.left + box.width / 2
+ 
+ // The room one leaves behind when it is lifted out of the row: its own width and
+ // the gap beside it, read off the row itself rather than from the class that set
+ // the gap, so nothing here has to be told the number twice.
+ export function room(boxes: Box[], from: number): number {
+   const held = boxes[from]
+   if (!held) return 0
+   const after = boxes[from + 1]
+   const before = boxes[from - 1]
+   const gap = after ? after.left - end(held) : before ? held.left - end(before) : 0
+   return held.width + gap
+ }
+ 
+ // Where one dragged dx from its own slot would land. The leading edge is what
+ // decides it rather than the middle: measured from the middle, a wide one has to
+ // travel its own width as well as the gap before it passes the narrow one beside
+ // it, which reads as a row that will not take what is being dragged into it.
+ export function landing(boxes: Box[], from: number, dx: number): number {
+   const held = boxes[from]
+   if (!held) return from
+   let to = from
+   boxes.forEach((box, index) => {
+     if (index > from && end(held) + dx > middle(box)) to = Math.max(to, index)
+     if (index < from && held.left + dx < middle(box)) to = Math.min(to, index)
+   })
+   return to
+ }
+ 
+ // How far the one standing at index steps aside while from is on its way to to.
+ // Everything the held one has passed moves back by the room it left behind, and
+ // every gap is the same width, so one number covers all of them.
+ export function shift(boxes: Box[], from: number, to: number, index: number): number {
+   if (index > from && index <= to) return -room(boxes, from)
+   if (index < from && index >= to) return room(boxes, from)
+   return 0
+ }

+ import { useRef, type PointerEvent as Press } from 'react'
+ import { landing, shift, type Box } from './reorder'
+ 
+ // How far the pointer travels before the row believes it is a drag rather than a
+ // press, so a plain click still lands on whatever it was aimed at.
+ const TAKES = 4
+ // A row that scrolls carries itself along while something is held near either end
+ // of it, or the far end is somewhere nothing can be dropped.
+ const EDGE = 56
+ const STEP = 12
+ const SLIDE = 'translate 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)'
+ 
+ export type Reorder = {
+   ref: (node: HTMLElement | null) => void
+   take(id: string): (event: Press) => void
+   dragged(): boolean
+ }
+ 
+ // Dragging one of a row of things into another place in it. Where each one goes
+ // is written straight onto the elements rather than held in state, the way the
+ // music's bars are: it runs every frame, and a render a frame would cost
+ // everything standing beside the row. Nothing is reordered until it is let go,
+ // so the row under the pointer stands still while it is being aimed at.
+ export function useReorder(onMove: (id: string, to: number) => void): Reorder {
+   const row = useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null)
+   const dragged = useRef(false)
+ 
+   const take = (id: string) => (event: Press) => {
+     const strip = row.current
+     if (event.button !== 0 || !strip) return
+     const bar = strip.getBoundingClientRect()
+     const items = Array.from(strip.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-reorder]'))
+     const from = items.findIndex(item => item.dataset.reorder === id)
+     const held = items[from]
+     if (!held || items.length < 2) return
+ 
+     // Boxes are read in the row's own coordinates rather than the window's, so a
+     // row that scrolls under a drag does not put every one of them out.
+     const boxes: Box[] = items.map(item => {
+       const box = item.getBoundingClientRect()
+       return { left: box.left - bar.left + strip.scrollLeft, width: box.width }
+     })
+     const startX = event.clientX - bar.left + strip.scrollLeft
+ 
+     let pointer = event.clientX
+     let taken = false
+     let to = from
+     let frame = 0
+     dragged.current = false
+ 
+     const tick = () => {
+       const dx = pointer - bar.left + strip.scrollLeft - startX
+       if (!taken && Math.abs(dx) < TAKES) return
+       taken = true
+       dragged.current = true
+       held.style.translate = `${dx}px`
+       held.style.zIndex = '10'
+       held.style.cursor = 'grabbing'
+       const next = landing(boxes, from, dx)
+       if (next === to) return
+       to = next
+       items.forEach((item, index) => {
+         if (index === from) return
+         item.style.transition = SLIDE
+         item.style.translate = `${shift(boxes, from, to, index)}px`
+       })
+     }
+ 
+     // The pointer standing still near an end still carries the row along, so the
+     // reading happens on a frame of its own as well as on every move.
+     const draw = () => {
+       frame = requestAnimationFrame(draw)
+       const past = pointer - bar.left
+       if (past < EDGE) strip.scrollLeft -= STEP
+       else if (past > bar.width - EDGE) strip.scrollLeft += STEP
+       tick()
+     }
+ 
+     const move = (moved: PointerEvent) => {
+       pointer = moved.clientX
+       tick()
+     }
+ 
+     // Everything the drag wrote is taken off before the row is reordered, and
+     // the transition goes with it, or the one that was let go slides in from a
+     // slot it has already left.
+     const stop = (keep: boolean) => {
+       cancelAnimationFrame(frame)
+       window.removeEventListener('pointermove', move)
+       window.removeEventListener('pointerup', up)
+       window.removeEventListener('pointercancel', cancel)
+       window.removeEventListener('keydown', key)
+       items.forEach(item => {
+         item.style.translate = ''
+         item.style.transition = ''
+         item.style.zIndex = ''
+         item.style.cursor = ''
+       })
+       if (keep && to !== from) onMove(id, to)
+     }
+ 
+     const up = () => stop(true)
+     const cancel = () => stop(false)
+     const key = (pressed: KeyboardEvent) => {
+       if (pressed.key === 'Escape') stop(false)
+     }
+ 
+     window.addEventListener('pointermove', move)
+     window.addEventListener('pointerup', up)
+     window.addEventListener('pointercancel', cancel)
+     window.addEventListener('keydown', key)
+     frame = requestAnimationFrame(draw)
+   }
+ 
+   return {
+     ref: node => {
+       row.current = node
+     },
+     take,
+     dragged: () => dragged.current
+   }
+ }
